text.content:
Storyteller-facing detail on torpor duration, staking, and blood deterioration — useful for adjudicating captured or besieged vampires in a Dark Ages chronicle.

Entering and Leaving Torpor

A Cainite can enter torpor voluntarily (a few seconds, no challenge), through injury (pushed past Incapacitated by lethal damage), or through deterioration (see below). A vampire who entered torpor voluntarily may attempt to rise after only half the duration below; one who entered through injury or deterioration must sleep the full term.

Road RatingTorpor Duration
Very lowTwo days
LowOne week
ModerateOne year
HighOne decade
Very highOne century
ExceptionalOne millennium

Lower Road ratings sleep deeper and longer. After the appropriate rest, the player spends a Blood Trait and attempts a Static Mental Challenge (difficulty three); failure means another attempt (and another spent Blood Trait) the following night, and a vampire with no blood cannot rise until fed. A vampire who entered torpor from blood loss specifically may rise as soon as she is fed at least one Blood Trait, regardless of Road rating ("early revivification"); this exception does not apply to those who entered voluntarily or through injury. A vampire rising with fewer than three Blood Traits must check for frenzy; one rising after full deterioration frenzies automatically.

Staking

A stake through the heart totally paralyzes a vampire — no movement, no blood expenditure, no Discipline activation — though she remains conscious, aware, and sensory (subject to whatever impairment her position causes). She must still spend blood to awaken nightly, risking deterioration. Placing a stake successfully requires two successful (win or tie) Simple Tests following a successful stake attack; if the target is mobile and defending, the Storyteller may require outright wins on both tests instead. On removal, the victim must win a Self-Control/Instinct Challenge (difficulty two, higher for long confinement or threatening events during it) to avoid immediate frenzy.

Deterioration

Deterioration happens to vampires denied blood for extended periods — most often staked victims who must still spend blood nightly, but also anyone trapped without a feeding opportunity. For each situation requiring a Blood Trait expenditure that a starved vampire cannot pay, she suffers one level of lethal damage and loses one appearance-related Social Trait (or gains the Negative Trait Withered once such Traits run out) until she reaches torpor. Reaching Incapacitated leaves her a husk; further deterioration pushes her into torpor, ending the pain but making revival harder (requires being fed blood directly; any blood placed in her mouth is consumed and heals her as fast as her generation allows). It's possible to keep a staked, deteriorating Cainite hovering just above Incapacitated indefinitely with careful blood-dosing — a favored, quietly horrific interrogation or imprisonment technique that often leaves the victim with derangements from the prolonged torment.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Five: Rules, Systems and Drama
